Container.Name: kb-litellm
Container.Overview: The model router for the knowledge stack: one OpenAI-style endpoint in front of local models and paid providers, with fallbacks, virtual keys and per-provider spend caps. STARTED IN ORDER: kb-postgres, then kb-redis, then kb-litellm, then kb-service, then kb-webui. There is no template equivalent of compose depends_on, so nothing enforces that for you. NOTHING WORKS UNTIL: (1) config.yaml lists models - LiteLLM does nothing useful until it does, and models are read from that file, not from the database; (2) a database named litellm exists on kb-postgres, created by hand first, because kb-postgres only creates the one database its own settings name; (3) kb-redis is up with the same password, because the budgets need it. NETWORK: the kb containers share one user-defined Docker network named kb that you create once, by hand, before the first start (a template cannot create a network, so Network stays bridge here - set it to kb when you create the container). Docker must preserve user-defined networks across updates (Unraid: Settings > Docker, Preserve user defined networks = Yes), or the containers fall back to bridge and the container names stop resolving. EXPOSURE: this container is exposed on your LAN through the host port you choose, behind the master key and virtual keys; anything further (a domain, reverse proxy, TLS) is a separate step for whoever administers your network. The admin UI is at /ui on that port; the link above is the unauthenticated liveness route. CONFIG: the config file is mounted read-only at /app/config.yaml and Post Arguments points the proxy at it; leave Post Arguments as shipped. A change to config.yaml takes effect when the container is restarted. KEYS: LITELLM_SALT_KEY encrypts the provider credentials stored in the database - set it once and never change it. Provider keys are optional and masked; leave a provider blank until you add it to config.yaml. The process runs as root inside the container (the image has no non-root build). IMAGE TAG: pinned to one release; an Update is a deliberate bump of that pin.
Container.Description: Model router for the knowledge stack (local models plus paid providers, with spend caps). Start after kb-postgres and kb-redis, before kb-service. LAN-exposed; needs a config.yaml that lists models and its own litellm database.

Config.Name: HTTP Port
Config.Description: REQUIRED. Host port for LiteLLM (API, /ui admin page and /health/liveness); the container always listens on 4000 internally - change the host side only. No default is offered: pick a free port.

Config.Name: config.yaml
Config.Description: REQUIRED. The proxy configuration file: the model list, routing, budgets and cache settings. Set an absolute path to the FILE, e.g. /mnt/<pool>/appdata/kb-litellm/config.yaml. Mounted read-only; edit it on the host and restart the container. LiteLLM does nothing until it lists models. Reference a secret as os.environ/<VARIABLE>, never as a literal.

Config.Name: LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
Config.Description: REQUIRED. Administrator key for the proxy API. Use a long random value starting sk- (upstream's own generator makes sk- plus 64 hex digits). The proxy refuses to start when this is blank or the published example sk-1234.

Config.Name: DATABASE_URL
Config.Description: REQUIRED. PostgreSQL connection URL, format postgresql://<user>:<password>@kb-postgres:5432/litellm - the user and password set on kb-postgres, the host being its container name on the kb network, and the litellm database created by hand beforehand. Percent-encode any reserved character in the password.

Config.Name: LITELLM_SALT_KEY
Config.Description: REQUIRED. Encrypts the provider credentials stored in the database. Set it once and NEVER change it: after a change those credentials can no longer be decrypted. Use a long random value and keep a copy.

Config.Name: REDIS_HOST
Config.Description: Redis host for budgets and cache: the container name of kb-redis on the kb network. Leave kb-redis.

Config.Name: REDIS_PASSWORD
Config.Description: REQUIRED. The password set on kb-redis; the same value.

Config.Name: UI_USERNAME
Config.Description: Username for the admin UI at /ui. Upstream's own default is admin; a blank value would be an empty username, so it ships admin.

Config.Name: UI_PASSWORD
Config.Description: REQUIRED. Password for the admin UI at /ui. Use a long random value. Never leave it blank: a blank Variable is an EMPTY password, not an unset one, so the master key would not be the fallback.

Config.Name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
Config.Description: Anthropic API key. Optional; leave blank until an Anthropic model is listed in config.yaml, which then names it as os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

Config.Name: XAI_API_KEY
Config.Description: xAI (Grok) API key. Optional; leave blank until an xAI model is listed in config.yaml.

Config.Name: GEMINI_API_KEY
Config.Description: Google Gemini API key. Optional; leave blank until a Gemini model is listed in config.yaml.

Config.Name: PERPLEXITYAI_API_KEY
Config.Description: Perplexity API key. Optional; leave blank until a Perplexity model is listed in config.yaml.

Config.Name: GROQ_API_KEY
Config.Description: Groq API key. Optional; leave blank until a Groq model is listed in config.yaml.

Config.Name: CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY
Config.Description: Cloudflare API token for Workers AI. Optional; leave blank until a Cloudflare model is listed in config.yaml.

Config.Name: CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID
Config.Description: Cloudflare account ID, the path segment of the Workers AI endpoint. Optional; leave blank until a Cloudflare model is listed in config.yaml.

Config.Name: LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP
Config.Description: Use the price list bundled in the image, so the container fetches nothing from GitHub at start. Leave True. Set False to fetch the current list at start.
